evidence: The reviewer named a real exposure (encodeSBOM relies on EncodeVersion downgrade, the path upstream changed) but itself judged regression unlikely and asked only for verification; no defect existed. The agent ran TestWriteSBOMWireContract and the full tools/licenses suite against the merge result and reported PASS, which is the evidence asked for, and made no code change.

The sub-delimiter encoding change could in principle move the pinned `%2B` purl, but the agent showed TestWriteSBOMComponentFields still passes at sbom_test.go:183 under v0.1.7, and correctly noted `-` and `.` are RFC 3986 unreserved, not sub-delims. Risk flagged, no defect present.

narrative: Dependabot bump of six Go modules. Round 1 raised two verify-before-merge concerns about cyclonedx-go downgrade behavior and packageurl-go sub-delimiter encoding, each tied to a specific pinned test. The agent verified both against the merge result rather than the stale branch CI and resolved with test evidence; no code changed and no finding came from a fix.
guidance_observations: Verifying a dependency bump against the merge result (master plus branch) rather than the branch's 11-day-old CI is the right move and is worth keeping as standard practice for dependabot PRs.

evidence: The hunk shows the doc comment claiming "in both directions" while the body only loops storage.SortFields asserting acceptance. The agent added the reverse direction with six near-miss field names and a per-probe precondition, which closes the hole rather than narrowing the comment.
guidance_note: Before committing a test whose doc comment names the failure modes it catches, check that each named failure mode has an assertion in the body.

evidence: Duplicate of F1 on the same hunk: the comment claims both directions, the loop checks one. Covered by the same fix in fac4bc6.
guidance_note: Before committing a test whose doc comment names the failure modes it catches, check that each named failure mode has an assertion in the body.

evidence: Third duplicate of F1; same verified gap between the "both directions" comment and an acceptance-only loop, fixed in fac4bc6.
guidance_note: Before committing a test whose doc comment names the failure modes it catches, check that each named failure mode has an assertion in the body.

evidence: Fourth duplicate of F1, also noting the case name and CHANGELOG bullet make the same both-directions claim; the reverse-direction probe added in fac4bc6 makes all three true.
guidance_note: Before committing a test whose doc comment names the failure modes it catches, check that each named failure mode has an assertion in the body.

evidence: The PR flipped both behaviors memory/doc.go described as "deliberately answers better than Dolt" (status sort and event ordering) without touching doc.go. The agent rewrote both bullets and in the same sweep found a third stale claim in conformance.go's package doc.
guidance_note: When a change flips an engine's documented behavior, grep the package doc and sibling docs for the old behavior's description before pushing.

evidence: ListAllEvents now sorted via sortEvents while Export still used raw cloneEvents(e.events), diverging from Dolt's Export, which goes through ListAllEvents. The agent took the reviewer's first option (sortEvents in Export), correctly rejected the alternative because calling ListAllEvents under the held non-reentrant mutex deadlocks, and forced same-tick ties so the test is not vacuous.
guidance_note: When introducing a helper documented as the one place an ordering is enforced, grep every reader of the underlying collection in the package and route each through it.

evidence: `built (v0.9.0)` asserted a version with no tag while the work sat under [Unreleased]. The agent first resolved it as invalid, arguing next-version.sh determinism, then retracted and fixed it a different way: a `built (unreleased)` status plus a RELEASING.md step. Reply 3 then corrected that RELEASING.md wording in f644776, because taken literally it would have flipped the convention's own definitions.
guidance_note: Before asserting a version number in docs, check that a tag carries it; a value computed by a script from present state is a prediction, not a fact the repo holds.

evidence: Same stale memory/doc.go status-sort bullet as F5, raised against compareStoredStatus; the doc.go rewrite in fac4bc6 covers it.
guidance_note: When a change flips an engine's documented behavior, grep the package doc and sibling docs for the old behavior's description before pushing.

evidence: Same stale memory/doc.go history-ordering bullet as F5, raised against ListAllEvents; fixed by the same rewrite.
guidance_note: When a change flips an engine's documented behavior, grep the package doc and sibling docs for the old behavior's description before pushing.

narrative: Round 0 raised nine findings that collapse to four issues: a test comment claiming two directions while checking one (x4), stale memory/doc.go claims after a behavior flip (x3), a real Export ordering bug, and a doc asserting an untagged v0.9.0. All were fixed in one commit and round 1 was clean. The agent's first pushback on F7 was wrong and was retracted within the round; a follow-up commit then fixed a defect in the agent's own new RELEASING.md instruction before any reviewer saw it.
guidance_observations: Three of four distinct issues are 'a claim in prose that the code does not back' (test comment, package doc, version status); a pre-push pass that reads each new or touched doc claim against the code would have caught all three.

The agent's self-audit after its own fix (reply 3 on F7) caught that an instruction would mechanically destroy the convention it served; doing that same literal-execution check before the first push would have spared the retraction.

evidence: The PR title says the file deliberately captures a conversation, and PR #406 and links-claims-1ihf are this repo's own PR and lit ticket, so "don't exist in this repo" is wrong. The doc's rule 5 is about claims on current code, not cross-references. Merged at 08:48:59, before the 08:54 review, and the thread was never answered.
guidance_note: Do not merge a PR before its automated review posts; a 17-second create-to-merge leaves every finding unanswered.

evidence: The title ("capture the decomposition conversation") shows the transcript is intentional, so "strip it" is wrong. The kernel is real: at a guidance-sounding path (docs/how-to-write-docs.md) with no framing, a reader cannot tell it is a verbatim record. A one-line header saying so would answer it. The packet shows no reply.
guidance_note: When committing a verbatim transcript as a doc, open it with a line stating it is a captured record, and name the file accordingly, so readers and reviewers do not take it for authored guidance.

evidence: The contradiction is real: the closing line says "nothing above mentions event stores" while Stage 1 lists "(B) event store in shadow". But the file is a captured conversation, and editing its content would falsify the record. Unanswered.
The second-person address is inherent to a captured conversation, which the PR title says this file is. Rewriting it into third person would make it something other than the record. Unanswered.

The ★ Insight box is part of the captured chat output; given the stated intent to capture the conversation, removing it is not called for, and [LAW:decomposition] does not bear on a doc's callout styling. Unanswered.
It is true the file has no markdown headings, but rule 3's "stable anchors" governs design docs, not a captured transcript, and [LAW:one-source-of-truth] does not apply. Unanswered.

The box-drawing table sits in bare markdown with no code fence, so GitHub will reflow it as a paragraph and garble it, even in a faithful transcript. The fix that keeps the record intact is to fence it, not convert it. The "chat artifact" framing and [LAW:decomposition] are off. Unanswered.
guidance_note: When pasting terminal-rendered output into markdown, wrap it in a code fence so whitespace-aligned layout survives rendering.

evidence: The dials sum to 160-200k, so "~200k" is the upper bound, not a midpoint. That is loose, but it matches the user's stated 200k ceiling inside a captured conversation, and "S2 Comment mismatch" overstates it. Unanswered.
The file lives in links-issue-tracker, the lit repository itself, so asking for a lit primer inside lit's own docs misreads the audience; [LAW:composability] does not apply. Unanswered.

narrative: A one-file docs PR that captures a chat transcript, merged 17 seconds after creation, about six minutes before the automated review posted nine findings (CHANGES_REQUESTED). No thread was ever answered. Most findings misread a deliberate transcript as authored guidance, but two had real kernels: the file carries no framing saying it is a record, and an unfenced box-drawing table renders garbled.
guidance_observations: Merging before the review lands converts every finding, including the two real ones, into silent debt; the merge should wait for the review and its threads should be answered even when most findings are wrong.
The reviewer had no signal that the file was intentionally a transcript beyond the PR title; a framing line in the file would have prevented most of the nine findings.

evidence: payload["maintenance"] was set but printSyncPushPayload's early-return cascade never read it, and the finding also named the traceMetadata omission. The agent hoisted the print, which was right, but argued the trace out on a "second subject" ground. It reversed that on F17 after conceding result.Message is already in traceMetadata and hook stdout goes unwatched.
guidance_note: When adding a field meant to reach the operator, trace every sink the sibling field reaches (stdout renderer and durable trace) and add a test that asserts the value at each sink.

evidence: The test comment said 90 MB while the CHANGELOG and package doc said 97 MB. The agent explained that the mirror grew during the session and corrected the comment.
guidance_note: When a measured figure is quoted in several places, update every quotation in the same pass after the final measurement; grep for the old number.

evidence: This finding asked only that printSyncPushPayload print the maintenance key, and the hoisted print with a both-modes test does exactly that. The agent's decision to keep pushOutcomeRecord unchanged is sound: that record answers whether the push landed.
guidance_note: When adding a field meant to reach the operator, add a test that asserts it appears in rendered output, not just in the payload map.

evidence: This duplicates the rendering gap: the verbose branch returns on raw before reaching maintenance. The fix in 5405394 hoisted the print above the cascade and pinned it in both modes.
guidance_note: When adding a field meant to reach the operator, add a test that asserts it appears in rendered output, not just in the payload map.

evidence: String() returned "nothing abandoned" on every routine run, which contradicted the "empty when it did nothing" doc and made the guard always true. The agent took the reviewer's second option (empty at the source) and pinned that every actionable state renders non-empty.
guidance_note: When a doc states an emptiness contract, check the producer can actually return empty on the routine path before committing it.

evidence: This is the same rendering gap as F3 and F4, with a request for a test asserting output. The fix added TestPrintSyncPushPayloadSurfacesMaintenanceInBothModes.
guidance_note: When adding a field meant to reach the operator, add a test that asserts it appears in rendered output, not just in the payload map.

evidence: The finding explicitly asked for the print "and/or include it in traceMetadata" and noted a refusal is silently dropped. The agent fixed the print and argued the trace out, then conceded on F17 that the argument fails because result.Message is already in traceMetadata. The declined half became a round-1 finding.
guidance_note: When adding a field meant to reach the operator, trace every sink the sibling field reaches (stdout renderer and durable trace) and add a test that asserts the value at each sink.

evidence: This is the mirror image of F2: the CHANGELOG said 97 MB and the test comment said 90 MB. The stale side was the test comment, and that is what got corrected.
guidance_note: When a measured figure is quoted in several places, update every quotation in the same pass after the final measurement; grep for the old number.

evidence: The hunk shows String() checking Problem first and returning only the problem, which discards the Removed/Reclaimed values the loop accumulated before failing. The agent added a Problem&&Removed>0 arm and a test asserting all four facts survive.
guidance_note: When a result type carries both progress counters and an error, enumerate the combined state (progress then failure) in the renderer's switch before writing the arms.

evidence: This duplicates F9 (partial progress is dropped by String()'s first arm). It was fixed by the same Report() change in 5405394.
guidance_note: When a result type carries both progress counters and an error, enumerate the combined state (progress then failure) in the renderer's switch before writing the arms.

evidence: The prune ran an unbounded walk and delete inside the cross-process commit lock. Moving it out was a reasonable call, but the agent's safety argument ("unreachable by construction") ignored concurrent prune against prune and concurrent re-add of a remote. That produced F14 and F21 in later rounds.
guidance_note: When moving work out of a lock, list every concurrent actor the lock used to serialize against (sibling instances of the same operation included) and handle each before claiming it is safe without the lock.

evidence: This is a third duplicate of F9; same partial-progress loss, fixed by the same Report() arm and test.
guidance_note: When a result type carries both progress counters and an error, enumerate the combined state (progress then failure) in the renderer's switch before writing the arms.

evidence: The POST-REVIEW flag is a false positive. The "keyed on the LITERAL remote URL string" phrase is already in the round-0 CHANGELOG hunk shown under F8, so it predates review, and 3c9347c only touched remotecache.go's prune doc comment. The claim did contradict remoteCacheKey's normalization, and the agent fixed both the CHANGELOG and the same claim in the package doc.
guidance_note: When documenting a derived key, copy its description from the function that computes it rather than paraphrasing from memory.

evidence: With the prune moved outside the commit lock (the F11 fix), two explicit pushes could reach the prune loop together. One process's RemoveAll would then make the other's dirSize fail with ENOENT and report a false problem; the agent confirmed explicit pushes are not otherwise serialized. Treating not-exist as already-collected is the right fix, and it was mutation-checked.
guidance_note: When moving work out of a lock, list every concurrent actor the lock used to serialize against (sibling instances of the same operation included) and handle each before claiming it is safe without the lock.

evidence: The F1 fix's test used strings.Contains, which passes for any placement, while the fix and CHANGELOG both promise the line prints above the push line. The agent changed it to assert line 0 and line 1 per mode, and showed that moving the print into an arm now fails the test.
guidance_note: When a fix's stated purpose is a placement or ordering, assert the position in the test, not mere presence.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: planRemoteCachePrune's refusal gate is original round-0 code (the hunk is unchanged by 3c9347c, which only edited a doc comment). The premise holds, since an idle configured remote blocks pruning forever, but the agent's counter-example shows narrowing the gate to the pushed remote would delete another remote's live mirror under URL-shape drift. Fixing the message to name both causes plus a clearing action, and filing links-storage-bd8w.1.1, is the defensible answer.
guidance_note: When writing a refusal message for an ambiguous condition, list every cause that produces the condition rather than asserting the alarming one.

evidence: F7 (and F1) asked for the maintenance report in traceMetadata, and the agent declined. This round re-raised it with the pre-push-hook argument. The agent conceded its "second subject" reasoning failed because result.Message already lives in traceMetadata, and added the key.
guidance_note: When declining part of a finding, check the decline against how the sibling field is already handled; an exception the sibling does not get is a gap, not a design.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: the fail-fast `return outcome` in the loop is visible in the round-0 code (F11/F14 hunks) and was not introduced by 3c9347c. The premise is true, since a sorted plan makes one stuck directory a permanent blocker. The agent switched to accumulating problems and continuing, with a mutation-verified chmod test.
guidance_note: When a loop processes a deterministically ordered list on every run, make per-item failures continue rather than return, or one stuck item blocks all later ones forever.

evidence: The F14 fix closed the ENOENT window at dirSize but not the gap before RemoveAll, which returns nil on a missing path and so double-counts reclaimed bytes. The agent confirmed this, then declined rename-as-claim because a crash would strand residue that nothing collects, documented the window in the doc comment, and recorded it on links-storage-bd8w.1.1. For a reporting-only inaccuracy that trade is sound.
guidance_note: When fixing one concurrency window in a check-then-act sequence, walk every later step of the same sequence for the same interleaving before pushing.

evidence: The F17 fix added traceMetadata["maintenance"] untested, and the agent said so in its reply. Extracting syncPushTraceMetadata as a pure function made it testable without the fixture the reviewer proposed, and two tests now pin presence and absence.
guidance_note: When a new line is untestable where it sits, extract the job it belongs to into a pure function in the same fix rather than shipping it with a stated gap.

evidence: Under the commit lock, a concurrent re-add and push could not create a mirror mid-loop. Moving the prune out (the F11 fix) let a stale plan delete a mirror that came back to life, and the 3c9347c "unreachable by construction" comment only held at plan time, which the agent itself admits. The fix re-checks eligibility against a fresh remote list before each removal and was mutation-verified.
guidance_note: When moving work out of a lock, list every concurrent actor the lock used to serialize against (sibling instances of the same operation included) and handle each before claiming it is safe without the lock.

narrative: A remote-cache prune feature whose round-0 findings were real: the report never rendered, partial progress was dropped, the emptiness contract was false, and the prune held the commit lock. The lock move (F11) is the root of the costliest chain. Its "unreachable by construction" argument ignored sibling prunes and remotes revived mid-loop, yielding F14 and F21, and F14's partial fix yielded F19. Separately, the agent declined the trace half of F1/F7, which returned as F17, whose untested fix returned as F20. Round 1 also carried three pre-existing gaps (F13, F16, F18), so only round 2 was purely fix-caused.
guidance_observations: Every fix-caused finding in this PR traces back to one of two decisions: moving work out of a lock without enumerating concurrent actors, or declining half of a finding on reasoning the code's sibling handling already contradicted.

The agent mutation-checked its tests from round 1 onward and said so; the round-0 test for the F1 fix used strings.Contains and passed for the arrangement it was meant to rule out, which is what F15 caught.
Recording rejected-but-real findings (F16, F19) on a named follow-up ticket with the counter-example kept those rounds from repeating.
